lines.text: Garp didn't fail Ace at Marineford. He chose Luffy.

shot.fallback: old marine hero in a cape with a dog hat

lines.text: I know, the internet says he stood there and let his grandson die.
But watch what actually happens when Luffy charges at the scaffold.

shot.fallback: boy sprinting across a war zone

lines.text: Garp jumps in front of him and says he's a Marine Vice Admiral.

shot.fallback: old marine blocking a boy's path

lines.text: He tells Luffy he'll have to kill him to get to Ace.
And then, at the last second, Garp falters.
Luffy hits him and Garp doesn't hit back.

shot.fallback: old marine crashing into the ground

lines.text: A man who's fought pirates since before Luffy was born just let the pirate through.

shot.fallback: veteran marine looking down in shame

lines.text: People say he should have stopped Akainu instead. That's fair.
But look at what he does after Ace dies. He wants to kill Akainu.
It's Sengoku who has to hold him back.
So the duty was never the real choice. It was the cage.

shot.fallback: old man weeping in the rain

lines.text: Garp didn't fail Ace at Marineford...

shot.fallback: old marine facing a young pirate

topic: At Marineford Garp refused to move for Luffy, then let Luffy hit him: the Marine duty was his excuse, not his choice
title: Garp Didn't Fail Ace At Marineford, He Chose Luffy
description: Everyone says Garp let Ace die for his duty. Look closer at what he did when Luffy ran at him, and what he wanted to do to Akainu after. Does Garp deserve the hate, or was he stuck in an impossible spot?
comment: Did Garp fail Ace at Marineford, or did he do the only thing a Marine grandfather could? Pick one.

self_check.loop: last line completes the first sentence
